page_note: Page divides cleanly: segments 0-23 are an extended hagiographic-narrative frame (the apostle and his disciples observing the lions invading the city walls along the Tigris, a disciple marveling at the phenomenon), with the seam flag at i=19 ('Then the apostle said') marking the pivot to substrate teaching. Segments 24-36 contain the cosmological teaching proper: the First Man bearing the elements, standing against the first Enmity in the Darkness, the great Archons receiving the 'garment of the lions' — a clear cosmological-correspondential substrate explaining the mythic origin of the Tigris-lions phenomenon in the 'first appointed time.' The narrative frame is unusually long here because it serves to motivate the teaching question. Segment 32 contains an internal citation to 'the great Gospel' (likely Mani's Living Gospel), an editorial seam. Page is heavily damaged (54%), so much of the substrate teaching is fragmentary.
